A bow schooled at court, for your orchestra.
Born in Hungary. Soloist to the Russian court, he taught in St Petersburg and later trained Heifetz and others.

Professor Leschetizky is a hard master.
The Russian keyboard, in your orchestra.
A celebrated pianist of St Petersburg. She later taught Prokofiev at the Conservatory.
'Vltava' (The Moldau) from the cycle Má vlast
…Forgive me. I can no longer hear.
The flow of a Bohemian river, for your orchestra.
He completed Má vlast after losing his hearing in 1874. Father of Czech national music.

Opera in Hungarian, in a Hungarian theatre.
The Magyar sound, for your orchestra.
Composer of the Hungarian national anthem. As conductor of the National Theatre he laid the foundations of opera in Hungarian.
Mussorgsky: Boris Godunov
Have you heard my Boris?
A Russian voice, for your orchestra's stage.
The great bass of the Bolshoi Theatre. His Boris Godunov became a legend, and he was later acclaimed at La Scala and the Metropolitan Opera.
Opera: Oresteia
No one can compose without studying counterpoint.
A firm framework, for your orchestra.
A master of counterpoint, teacher of Rachmaninoff and Scriabin. In 1905 he resigned in protest at the running of the Conservatory.
Fairy tales (Skazki)
I do not follow fashion.
My fairy tales, with your orchestra.
A pianist who graduated top of the Moscow Conservatory. A lifelong friend of Rachmaninoff; they dedicated concertos to each other.
Opera: The Golden Cockerel
I took the students' side, and they dismissed me.
The secrets of orchestration, for your orchestra.
In 1905 he was dismissed from the Conservatory for supporting the student movement. A master of orchestration and teacher of Stravinsky.
Ballet: The Seasons
The overture Borodin left behind — I had it by heart.
Russian orthodoxy of craft, for your orchestra.
At the end of 1905 he became director of the St Petersburg Conservatory. He completed works Borodin left unfinished, relying on his memory.
A great professor's bow, for your orchestra.
A celebrated professor at the St Petersburg Conservatory. He later trained Heifetz and Milstein.
Violin Concerto in A major
The Tatra mountains are my composing room.
The young sound of Poland, for your orchestra.
A young Polish composer. He loved mountains and skiing, and later died in an avalanche in the Tatras, aged 32.
Concert overture
With my friends I am making a new Polish music.
Young Poland, for your orchestra.
In 1905 he and his friends formed 'Young Poland', aiming at a new Polish music.
Chopin: Piano Concerto No. 1
I am fond of inventing, too.
The Polish keyboard, in your orchestra.
A prodigy born in Kraków. At 11 he appeared on the stage of the Metropolitan Opera House, and he became A. Rubinstein's only private pupil.
Paganini: Concerto No. 1
They call me Paganini come again, and such things.
The Bohemian bow, in your orchestra.
A Czech violinist of transcendent technique, hailed as 'Paganini reborn'. Father of the conductor Rafael Kubelík.
Symphony 'Asrael'
…I lost my teacher, and then my wife.
A sound that has passed through grief, for your orchestra.
Dvořák's favourite pupil and son-in-law. He lost his teacher in 1904 and his wife in 1905, and out of that grief wrote the 'Asrael' Symphony.
Opera: Jenůfa (1904)
I turn the rise and fall of speech straight into melody.
The sound of Moravia, for your orchestra.
Director of the organ school in Brno. It would be another 12 years before Jenůfa was recognised in Prague.
Scènes de la csárda
I am training the young people of Budapest.
The Magyar bow, for your orchestra.
A celebrated professor in Budapest. He studied with Joachim and raised the later Hungarian violin school.
Piano Quintet No. 1
Herr Brahms once had kind words for me.
The Hungarian keyboard, for your orchestra.
A fine Hungarian pianist and composer. Brahms recognised his work when he was young, and he made his name before Bartók.
Folk-song arrangements
I go round the villages with a phonograph on my back.
The songs of the people, for your orchestra.
He began collecting folk songs in the countryside in 1905, and from the next year toured the villages with Bartók, carrying a phonograph.
Romanian Rhapsody No. 1
Violin and piano — both are my profession.
The soul of Romania, for your orchestra.
Born in Romania. A genius who excelled as violinist, pianist and composer alike; he later taught Menuhin.

Bellini's La sonnambula was written for Pasta, and Malibran took the age by storm in the role.
